focus: Audit remaining central /doctor and skill-advisor lifecycle flows for answer-dependent branching, later-turn goal injection, and one-time session cleanup.
keyQuestions: Which remaining packages outside deep-loop contain genuinely answer-dependent or user-visible restart/compaction scenarios?
Which skill or mode behaviors involving questions, user answers, restart, compaction or runtime parity have no scenario that covers them?
Which conversion, update and coverage candidates provide the highest operator or release risk reduction for their authoring and execution cost?
answeredQuestions: Which /doctor question-tool flow has the clearest low-risk Q2 conversation script?
Which approval flows should be prioritized by safety, rollback and execution cost?
Which OpenCode goal/session-cleanup features need later-turn JSON coverage?

label: Convert central `/doctor:skill-advisor` DOC-367 into a JSON conversation for the safe menu branches: no target, X cancel, invalid answer twice, H help, then a test-only numeric target. Every answer changes the next displayed state or status, so Q2 is yes; runner question matching and scripted replies can test the menu without guessing. Keep unknown-target/cross-target command-line failures and any target that launches a mutating workflow as existing isolated checks.

Treat DOC-370 git-hook switch, DOC-372 standards edit, DOC-359 release update, and DOC-394 CI toggle as Q2 because no/approve answers determine writes, follow-up questions, and rollback. Add conversation coverage first for DOC-370 in a disposable checkout; DOC-372 and DOC-359 are higher value but need fixture setup and rollback checks; DOC-394 should cover only the safe declined branch unless its credentialed remote write can be isolated and restored.

Update both system-skill-advisor CL-007 and system-spec-kit goal-opencode-plugin coverage with a two-turn OpenCode JSON companion: set or bind an isolated goal, then send a later task request and verify the active-goal prompt is injected; add pause/resume only if the same state checks remain clear. Q2 is yes because the goal is per-session state and the requirement is model-visible context on a subsequent prompt, while both current contracts emphasize command/status output and injection preview.

Update system-spec-kit session-cleanup-plugin with a bounded OpenCode conversation companion: first send verifies the startup guard appears in model context, a second send proves it is delivered only once, and session restart/end checks cleanup behavior. Q2 applies to the session-created/injected/disposed lifecycle, but preserve the existing real-script and Claude SessionEnd evidence because the shared runner restart alone does not prove every teardown command.

Keep DOC-403 sk-skill-convert dry-run, DOC-390 unrelated no-hint, and one-prompt command plans single prompt. They explicitly ask nothing or invoke the hook once and produce a deterministic report; no scripted user reply changes what happens next, so Q4 applies. The numeric menu and approval cases above are the exceptions because their answer controls the flow.
